newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lifts restrictions for foreign insurers.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lifts restrictions for foreign insurers.

text.p: Foreign insurance companies can set up branches in Bulgaria under amendments to an insurance law passed on final reading by parliament on Wednesday.
"The law treats on equal footing domestic and international insurers who wish to operate in Bulgaria through branches," the head of parliament's budget comittee Yordan Tsonev told reporters.
Foreign insurers could participate in the local market only in joint ventures with local insurers according to a previous law, adopted last year.

Under the amendments insurance companies are expected to register in a National Insurance Council which will be headed by the finance minister and is authorised to extend or retract insurance licences.
Parliament increased tenfold the capital requirements for licensing insurance firms in order to provide a stable insurance market.

The minimum capital requirement for life insurance companies rises from 200 million levs to two billion levs, for property insurance companies from 300 million levs to three billion levs and reinsurance firms from 400 million levs to four billion levs.
Existing insurance companies are due to meet the new capital requirements until March 31, 1998.
"We have extended the licensing term to allow the existing companies to boost their capital through the profit, which they will post for 1997," Tsonev said.

Some 100 insurance companies operate in the country now, but economists predict that very few will be able to meet the new capital requirements, due to a sharp depreciation of the local currency which eroded their capital earlier this year.
The amendments also ban insurance companies from providing security services in a bid to clear the market from security firms, involved in racketeering, Tsonev said.
Many security firms, set up by former security services employees are currently registered as insurance companies and are involved in racketeering.

The NIC is expected to approve acquisition of stakes higher than five percent in insurnce firms by individuals or firms. Shareholders holding more than one percent stake will be required to verify the origin of their investment and their financial status.
The amendments are being voted item by item and parliament is expected to complete its final voting this week. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-981-4145
